*El video de **A-HA “The Sun Always Shines On T.V.”** se asume como la **continuación (o epílogo)** del video **“Take On Me”**.
Ambos fueron dirigidos por Steve Barron y están conectados narrativamente: el inicio de *The Sun Always Shines on T.V.* muestra a los mismos personajes de *Take On Me*, reencontrándose después de los eventos del primer video. Sin embargo, él vuelve a convertirse en dibujo y regresa a su mundo animado, marcando un final más melancólico para la historia.
Este video, junto con *Take On Me* y *Train of Thought*, forma parte de una **trilogía visual** que mezcla animación, realidad y simbolismo emocional característico de A-HA en los años 80.

---

The video for **A-HA’s “The Sun Always Shines On T.V.”** is widely considered to be the **continuation (or epilogue)** of the video **“Take On Me.”**
Both videos were directed by Steve Barron and share a narrative connection: the opening of *The Sun Always Shines on T.V.* features the same characters from *Take On Me*, meeting again after the events of the first video. However, he transforms back into a drawing and returns to his animated world, giving the story a more melancholic ending.
This video, together with *Take On Me* and *Train of Thought*, is part of a **visual trilogy** that blends animation, live action, and emotional symbolism—one of A-HA’s signature artistic approaches in the 1980s.
